title: Network People Services Technologies Ltd - 544396 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: NPSC Q2 FY27 consolidated income rose about 50% YoY to Rs 72.95 crore; management reiterated guidance with H2 growth expected.
summary.overview: Management reported consolidated income of about Rs 72.95 crore for Q2, up roughly 50% YoY and about 20% QoQ from Rs 61 crore in Q1. EBITDA was about Rs 16 crore, up about 17% YoY and 15% QoQ, while H1 revenue was cited at about Rs 134 crore (up about 60% YoY) and EPS at Rs 11.63. Management said ESP-related revenue now makes up about 80-85% of the business, against 15-20% two years ago, and that H1 was planned as an execution-heavy period with growth expected in H2. The call was heavy on pipeline claims (Sri Lanka telecom deal, a central bank-in-a-box LOI) with few hard numbers on contract value or timing.

financial_highlights.change: about +50% YoY from Rs 48.68 crore; about +20% QoQ from Rs 61 crore

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 28 crore (as stated by analyst; lower-margin revenue)

segments.name: ESP / TSP payments business
segments.commentary: Contribution has risen to about 80-85% of business from 15-20% two years ago, per management. Includes UPI, IMPS and bank-in-a-box offerings.

segments.name: International (Sri Lanka telecom deal, Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management says a multi-million-dollar Sri Lanka deal, five years, with about 20-25% one-time and 75-80% licence/recurring split; execution to start this quarter with about nine-month execution period, contribution from Q4 or Q1. Pipeline of 5-15 further international contracts cited.

segments.name: RegTech / compliance (DPDP, digital currency)
segments.commentary: Company says it won its first DPDP order from a private entity and its first digital currency order; no value disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated FY27 guidance; H1 described as execution-focused with growth expected in H2.
Sri Lanka deal: execution starts in Q3, contribution from Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28, meaningful numbers from FY28, cumulative growth in FY29 and FY30.
Domestic central bank-in-a-box LOI (value in 10-digit rupees, to be served over 18-24 months; company said direct revenue starts within about 9 months); five-year direct deal.
EBITDA margin: next quarter expected to be better than Q2; FY27 target about 25%; FY28 estimated at about 27-28%.
UPI MDR change (festive season or later) could add incremental value; management did not quantify it.
capex_capacity: Management said the Dubai subsidiary was formed to support international orders and that hardware inventory (licence and OEM product) was procured for project delivery.
Company said it has about 350 people (stated as more than 350).
Management said AI-led productivity improvement target of about 40%, with a new release by March.
Acquisition under consideration; not closed, no deal size disclosed. Funding said to come from existing funds, not new borrowing.
demand_pricing: Management says international buyers prefer mature solutions from India; pipeline of 5-15 additional international contracts (stages from discussions to RFPs).
Domestic growth driven by bank-in-a-box, plus a compliance-in-a-box product (DPDP, fraud) with subscription model; launch described as about a year ago.
Credit-on-UPI product is live technically, but banks have not yet adopted a revenue model; management said adoption is slow.
Management said the Sri Lanka deal is priced around 15x per-transaction revenue versus India (as stated on the call).

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue will the Sri Lanka telecom deal contribute, and what is the one-time vs recurring split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a split of about 20-25% one-time and 75-80% licence/recurring; described it as a multi-million-dollar deal over five years, with execution starting this quarter and contribution from Q4 or Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue break-up available by UPI switch, IMPS switch, bank-in-a-box?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue by product, saying the offerings are bundled and it is too early to disclose.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 growth still on track and any guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was always planned as slower due to execution and the Dubai subsidiary set-up; no change in guidance and confidence in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Operating margin trajectory and H2 operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 margin is somewhat lower than the previous half; management expects gradual improvement, with Q3 better than Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 300-bank deal contribute and for how long?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct deal is five years; direct revenue expected within about 9 months; further opportunity over the bank universe is open-ended.

qa_highlights.question: Will the acquisition need additional funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will use existing funds; deal size not disclosed as the deal is not closed.

risks_watch: Revenue mix very concentrated in payments/ESP; management has not disclosed product-level revenue.
Low-margin subsidiary revenue in Dubai weighed on margin in Q2; margin improvement is dependent on execution.
Sri Lanka and domestic bank-in-a-box contract values and timelines are not disclosed in figures; watch for Q3 and Q4 execution updates.
UPI MDR changes and bank adoption of credit-on-UPI revenue models remain unclear.
Undisclosed acquisition and the Biafara/Saksham scheme benefit not yet assessed by management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term pipeline and H2 growth, but evasive on hard numbers: deal values, product revenue split, and the acquisition size were not quantified. Several answers were loosely structured and repetitive, and the audio was often poor.
key_quotes: Our ESP revenue which contributed just about 15 to 20% of overall business two years back when we achieved our highest growth in the last four years. We have achieved about 80 to 85% in this quarter.
So there is no change in the guidelines.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance with H2 growth expected, but the call gave no quantified FY27 revenue target; the Sri Lanka deal and central bank LOI are pipeline claims without hard contract value or timing, and no capacity additions were disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin about 24% in Q2 with management saying Q3 will be better than Q2 and targeting about 25% for FY27, FY28 estimated at 27-28%; Dubai low-margin revenue weighed on Q2 and execution is the swing factor.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions disclosed; ~350 people and Dubai subsidiary formed to support international orders, with Sri Lanka execution starting Q3 and contribution from Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated H2 growth after H1 revenue of about Rs 134 crore (+60% YoY) and Q2 income of Rs 72.95 crore (+50% YoY, +20% QoQ), but gave no quantified FY27 revenue target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex not discussed; the only capital item is an undisclosed acquisition funded from existing cash.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was reiterated with no change and no quantified revenue target, and the Sri Lanka and central bank deal values are undisclosed, so there is no basis for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 was execution-heavy and margin ran about 24% against a 25% FY27 target, with Dubai low-margin revenue and undisclosed deal timelines as the main risks to H2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A new AI-led release is due by March, with a compliance-in-a-box (DPDP) product already in market and a first DPDP order and first digital currency order won, though no values were disclosed.

rows.label: Sri Lanka telecom deal execution
rows.when: Q3 FY27 start; revenue Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28
rows.why: Multi-million-dollar five-year deal, about 20-25% one-time and 75-80% recurring, with a roughly nine-month execution period starting this quarter; values still undisclosed.

rows.label: Domestic central bank-in-a-box LOI
rows.why: LOI value in 10-digit rupees, served over 18-24 months on a five-year direct deal, but the LOI is not yet a firm contract and no revenue figures were given.

rows.label: UPI MDR change
rows.why: Management said it could add incremental value but did not quantify it, and credit-on-UPI revenue models are not yet adopted by banks.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 growth, the Sri Lanka and central bank pipeline, and the ~25% FY27 margin target, but gave no hard deal values, product revenue split or acquisition size. Analysts pressed on the revenue split, deal size and margin trajectory, and the audio was poor.
